summary: BSP-based PetaLinux rebuild COMPLETE end-to-end: petalinux-create -s BSP -> MACHINE=xilinx-vck190 (confirmed board-specific via project-spec config) -> petalinux-config XSA overlay -> rootfs XRT/zocl enabled -> petalinux-build 4874 task PASS -> petalinux-build --sdk PASS -> SDK install to /tools/Xilinx/PetaLinux/2024.1/vck190_sdk_bsp -> cross-compile host_bsp.elf (471 KiB aarch64 ELF) -> v++ -p package_v4 PASS (sd_card.img + BOOT.BIN + launch_hw_emu.sh) -> qemu hw_emu launch PASS to Linux kernel 6.6.10. BUT kernel panics on rootfs mount: 'No filesystem could mount root, tried: ext3 ext2 ext4 cramfs vfat msdos iso9660 btrfs'. The kernel correctly SEES both mmcblk0p1 (488 MB) and mmcblk0p2 (280 MB) — the BSP fix DID work for partition addressing — but NO filesystem driver can mount p2. Root cause identified: Vitis-host's mkfs.ext4 (e2fsprogs ≥1.47) writes superblock features (metadata_csum_seed, orphan_file, fast_commit) that PetaLinux 2024.1 kernel's ext4 driver does not understand. This is a Vitis-tooling vs PetaLinux-kernel version-skew, NOT a BSP/template selection issue. T0042 analytic 160us remains published.
key_diagnostic_evidence: hw_emu_v4.log line [6.213134]: 'No filesystem could mount root, tried: ext3 ext2 ext4 cramfs vfat msdos iso9660 btrfs'. Combined with [6.212519]+[6.212816] showing mmcblk0p1+p2 both detected. Proves: partition addressing FIXED by BSP; rootfs FEATURE BLOB unrecognizable to kernel.
stages_passed_v4: qemu launch_hw_emu PASS to Linux kernel
kernel partition table parse: mmcblk0p1 + mmcblk0p2 detected
stages_blocked: ext4 rootfs mount on mmcblk0p2 (feature mismatch)
human_ack_reasons: Vitis 2024.1 mkfs.ext4 + PetaLinux 2024.1 kernel ext4 driver version-skew
Three attempts (template, prebuilt-image, BSP) all converge on this same lower-level tooling bug — definitively not fixable by autonomous worker
next_action_options: (A) Downgrade host's e2fsprogs / strip ext4 features with tune2fs before sd_card.img boot
(B) Boot from initramfs only (modify boot.scr to skip SD mount)
(C) Use BSP's pre-built petalinux-sdimage.wic.xz directly (known-good ext4)
